claim: Absolute TRAP_POSITION commands streamed from the host at 10 Hz move a Tweez 300 trap smoothly by eye.
validity_conditions:
One run of 61 commands tracing a circle and returning to 0 0; the person saw it move smoothly and end at the centre. 'Smoothly' is by eye on the GUI, not a measurement of position or timing; wall time was 6.016 s against 6.0 s planned, on the host clock. Record: D:/soft-matter-agents-frames/tweezers-20260924-001/exchanges.jsonl line 116.

The 100x objective was in the path and a sample was mounted -- both stated by the person after the commands. The trapping laser's emission was off -- also stated after the fact, and not logged before the first command. The GUI's calibrations were not stated, so NOTHING HERE IS A MICROMETRE: positions are GUI coordinates and moves are directions on screen. What this is: the person reading the GUI display.
